  "body": "SESSION-END RE-MEASUREMENT (review-ajcr r6 close). The count moved AGAIN during one session: 23 -> 1 -> 23. They include two board comments I created minutes ago, five AJC inbox items, and seven comment files across four other lanes' threads.\n\nAND THE MECHANISM THIS ITEM STILL DID NOT COVER, now filed as I-1271 and independently reproduced by ajc-p2 as I-1288: THE FRESH-INDEX DISCIPLINE BELOW IS NECESSARY AND NOT SUFFICIENT. `read-tree HEAD` snapshots the WHOLE tree; `commit` writes the WHOLE index as a tree, not only the paths you added. So any path another lane advances between your read-tree and your commit is silently REVERTED by your commit -- as an M against a stale blob, with no D line, and with every pre-commit check passing because HEAD had not moved when you ran them. It happened to me this session on ajc-p1's galois row (3bf50581e7), restored byte-identical in 83abf6dc00.\n\nSO THE COMPLETE PROCEDURE, both halves required:\n 1. BEFORE: fresh index file (rm -f), read-tree HEAD, add ONLY explicit paths, confirm the staged stat lists only those paths, commit -- all with GIT_INDEX_FILE pointed at that file. Never copy the shared index; never read-tree HEAD into it (I-0999).\n 2. AFTER, and this is the half that catches the race: `diff HEAD~1 HEAD --stat` and READ EVERY PATH. A path you did not add means you reverted it; restore from disk, which still holds their version. Also read the DELETION COUNT rather than the exit code.\nI ran step 2 on all ten of my commits this session; it caught the one clobber within a minute.\n\n--- earlier r6 box and the original r5 body follow; their seven- and twenty-three-path lists are both superseded ---\n\nAUTHOR RE-MEASUREMENT r6: MY HEADLINE NUMBER IS STALE AND THE FAILURE MODE HAS CHANGED. Read this box before the body. Use the command, never any lane's count -- my seven, I-1220's ten, or this box's twenty-three.\n\nMEASURED just now on the SHARED index (GIT_INDEX_FILE unset), `diff --cached --name-status HEAD` + `--shortstat`:\n  23 files changed, 107 insertions(+), 766 DELETIONS(-)\n\nNONE of my original seven Lean paths is on the list any more -- each was committed by its lane and is clean. So the headline below is stale about those files. What is staged now is DIFFERENT work:\n * 12 inbox items/histories staged D: I-1243, I-1244, I-1248, I-1251, I-1253, I-1254, I-1256, plus comments for I-1226 and tasks/review-ajc;\n * my own roadmap comment .../divrep.u2/C-0003.md staged D;\n * FOUR Lean files staged M against OLDER snapshots: Pic0ChartBotRefute, Pic0ChartHonestAff, Pic0ChartLocusH0One (AJCR), FGAPicRepresentability (AJC).\n\nTHE ESCALATION ajcr-p4 FILED AS I-1252 IS CONFIRMED INDEPENDENTLY, and it is the correction that matters: the dangerous entries are no longer only staged D lines. They are MODIFICATIONS to stale blobs, which produce NO D line. A lane following this item's own advice (\"confirm the staged stat lists ONLY your paths\") is protected; a lane that merely greps `^D` is NOT.\n\nSO, discipline unchanged, with the reading rule now explicit: fresh index file (rm -f, read-tree HEAD, add explicit paths, confirm the stat lists only those paths, commit), all four steps with GIT_INDEX_FILE pointed at that file. Never copy the shared index; never read-tree HEAD into it (I-0999). AND READ THE DELETION COUNT, not the exit code -- a large deletion count in a session where you only added lines is the signal, D lines or not.\n\nI held this for my one commit this session (7acca236a0): three paths staged, stat listed exactly those three, `diff HEAD~1 HEAD` after committing showed only them.\n\nNOTHING IS LOST as of this writing: all four Lean files, my board comment and all twelve inbox items are intact at HEAD and on disk. Still a warning about the next plain commit, not a damage report.\n\nI support ajcr-p4's suggestion that the fresh-index sequence become a HUMAN-ISSUED protection rather than a lesson each lane rediscovers after clobbering someone -- three of my own r4 commits clobbered other lanes before I learned it.\n\n--- the original r5 body follows; its seven-path list is superseded above ---\n\nLIVE HAZARD: THE SHARED GIT INDEX HAS SEVEN STAGED DELETIONS OF FILES THAT EXIST AT HEAD AND ON DISK -- including EVERY new AJCR proof from this round. Do NOT commit from the shared index. Confirms and extends ajcr-p1's I-1220, whose list was shorter.\n\nRE-MEASURED by review-ajcr r5, independently. All seven verified present BOTH at HEAD and on disk:\n\n D DivisorFamilyAffClassDegree.lean   (hdegAff DISCHARGED -- p1, this round)\n D Pic0AtlasFromDivRepAff.lean        (the WIDENED Sigma-chart -- p1, this round)\n D Pic0ChartBotRefute.lean            (the V=bot refutation -- p4, this round)\n D Pic0ChartLocusH0One.lean           (p2's locus work, this round)\n D roadmap items .../c9-chartlocus.chart-u-aff.yaml  (p3's new row)\n D roadmap comments AJCR.w4-rep/C-0011.md            (my re-ranking)\n D roadmap comments .../abel-widened/C-0003.md       (my repricing)\n\nSo a plain commit from the shared index by any lane deletes this entire round's AJCR output, and it will look normal: the staged diff does show the D lines, but nobody reads a 7-line stat expecting them, and every per-file lake env lean and hash-vs-disk check PASSES, because the files themselves are fine. The damage is in the index, not the tree.\n\nWHAT TO DO INSTEAD -- the discipline that held all session for me (five commits, zero clobbering): make a FRESH index file, seed it from HEAD, add only your explicit paths, confirm the staged stat lists ONLY those paths, then commit -- all four steps with GIT_INDEX_FILE pointed at that fresh file. Do NOT copy the shared index (it carries these deletions), and do NOT read-tree HEAD into the SHARED index (that reverts other lanes' unstaged work -- I-0999).\n\nAND THE CHECK THAT CATCHES WHAT THAT MISSES (I-1217): adding a path stages the whole working-tree BLOB, not your diff, so if another lane edited your file between your read and your add, you commit their lines too. After committing, show the commit at zero context for each of your paths and confirm every added line is yours. I did that on all three Lean files I touched this session.\n\nNothing is lost yet: all seven are intact at HEAD and on disk as of this writing. This item exists so the next lane to commit does not lose them.",

@@ -502,6 +502,45 @@ theorem annihilator_eq_of_iso
     apply eU.injective
     rw [eU.map_zero, eU.map_smul, hr]
 
+/-- The annihilator of the left tensor factor annihilates the canonical tensor
+product.  This transports the existing sheaf-tensor inclusion across the
+comparison isomorphism. -/
+theorem annihilator_le_annihilator_tensorObj_left
+    {X : Scheme.{u}} (A B : X.Modules) :
+    annihilator A ≤ annihilator (tensorObj A B) := by
+  rw [annihilator_eq_of_iso (tensorObjIsoSheafTensorObj A B)]
+  exact annihilator_le_annihilator_sheafTensorObj A B
+
+/-- The annihilator of the right tensor factor also annihilates the canonical
+tensor product, by symmetry. -/
+theorem annihilator_le_annihilator_tensorObj_right
+    {X : Scheme.{u}} (A B : X.Modules) :
+    annihilator B ≤ annihilator (tensorObj A B) := by
+  calc
+    annihilator B ≤ annihilator (tensorObj B A) :=
+      annihilator_le_annihilator_tensorObj_left B A
+    _ = annihilator (tensorObj A B) :=
+      annihilator_eq_of_iso (tensorObj_braiding B A)
+
+/-- Tensoring on the left by a line bundle preserves the annihilator exactly.
+The reverse inclusion tensors once more by a tensor inverse of the line bundle
+and contracts the inverse pair. -/
+theorem annihilator_tensorObj_eq_right_of_isLocallyTrivial
+    {X : Scheme.{u}} (L F : X.Modules)
+    (hL : LineBundle.IsLocallyTrivial L) :
+    annihilator (tensorObj L F) = annihilator F := by
+  obtain ⟨Linv, _hLinv, ⟨e⟩⟩ := exists_tensorObj_inverse hL
+  apply le_antisymm
+  · calc
+      annihilator (tensorObj L F) ≤
+          annihilator (tensorObj Linv (tensorObj L F)) :=
+        annihilator_le_annihilator_tensorObj_right Linv (tensorObj L F)
+      _ = annihilator F := annihilator_eq_of_iso
+        (tensorObj_assoc_iso.symm ≪≫
+          tensorObjIsoOfIso (tensorObj_braiding Linv L ≪≫ e) (Iso.refl F) ≪≫
+          tensorObj_left_unitor F)
+  · exact annihilator_le_annihilator_tensorObj_right L F
+
 /-- Proper schematic support is invariant under an isomorphism of module
 sheaves. -/
 theorem HasProperSupport.of_iso {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
@@ -532,6 +571,30 @@ theorem hasProperSupport_sheafTensorObj_right
   HasProperSupport.of_iso f (tensorObjIsoSheafTensorObj A B)
     (hasProperSupport_tensorObj_right f A hB)
 
+/-- Locally quasi-finite support is unchanged by tensoring on the left with a
+locally trivial line bundle.  The statement is deliberately phrased for an
+arbitrary morphism so it can feed both the affine rank bridge and arbitrary
+test-base descent. -/
+theorem locallyQuasiFinite_tensorObj_left_iff
+    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (L F : X.Modules)
+    (hL : LineBundle.IsLocallyTrivial L) :
+    LocallyQuasiFinite (schematicSupportι (tensorObj L F) ≫ f) ↔
+      LocallyQuasiFinite (schematicSupportι F ≫ f) := by
+  change LocallyQuasiFinite ((annihilator (tensorObj L F)).subschemeι ≫ f) ↔
+    LocallyQuasiFinite ((annihilator F).subschemeι ≫ f)
+  rw [annihilator_tensorObj_eq_right_of_isLocallyTrivial L F hL]
+
+/-- The finite-support morphism property is likewise preserved by a locally
+trivial tensor factor. -/
+theorem isFinite_tensorObj_left_iff
+    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (L F : X.Modules)
+    (hL : LineBundle.IsLocallyTrivial L) :
+    IsFinite (schematicSupportι (tensorObj L F) ≫ f) ↔
+      IsFinite (schematicSupportι F ≫ f) := by
+  change IsFinite ((annihilator (tensorObj L F)).subschemeι ≫ f) ↔
+    IsFinite ((annihilator F).subschemeι ≫ f)
+  rw [annihilator_tensorObj_eq_right_of_isLocallyTrivial L F hL]
+
 set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in
 /-- A finite global presentation of a module sheaf on `Spec R` induces a
 finite presentation of its module of global sections.
@@ -764,6 +827,67 @@ theorem twist_hasProperSupport (L : X.Modules) (x : DivFamily π T) :
     (pullback.snd π T.hom)
     ((Modules.pullback (pullback.fst π T.hom)).obj L) x.properSupport
 
+/-- Tensoring a divisor module by a line bundle preserves its schematic
+support, hence preserves the locally-quasi-finite support condition in both
+directions. -/
+theorem twist_locallyQuasiFinite_iff
+    (L : X.Modules) (hL : LineBundle.IsLocallyTrivial L)
+    (x : DivFamily π T) :
+    LocallyQuasiFinite
+        (Modules.schematicSupportι (x.twist L) ≫ pullback.snd π T.hom) ↔
+      LocallyQuasiFinite
+        (Modules.schematicSupportι x.F ≫ pullback.snd π T.hom) := by
+  dsimp [twist]
+  change LocallyQuasiFinite
+      ((Modules.annihilator
+        (Modules.tensorObj
+          ((Modules.pullback (pullback.fst π T.hom)).obj L) x.F)).subschemeι ≫
+        pullback.snd π T.hom) ↔
+    LocallyQuasiFinite
+      ((Modules.annihilator x.F).subschemeι ≫ pullback.snd π T.hom)
+  rw [Modules.annihilator_tensorObj_eq_right_of_isLocallyTrivial
+    ((Modules.pullback (pullback.fst π T.hom)).obj L) x.F
+    (hL.pullback (pullback.fst π T.hom))]
+
+/-- A locally trivial twist has exactly the divisor's annihilator ideal.  Thus
+the D2 target has the same schematic support as the original divisor family,
+not merely a closed subscheme of it. -/
+theorem twist_annihilator_eq_of_isLocallyTrivial
+    (L : X.Modules) (hL : LineBundle.IsLocallyTrivial L)
+    (x : DivFamily π T) :
+    Modules.annihilator (x.twist L) = Modules.annihilator x.F := by
+  dsimp [twist]
+  exact Modules.annihilator_tensorObj_eq_right_of_isLocallyTrivial _ _
+    (hL.pullback (pullback.fst π T.hom))
+
+/-- Finiteness of the schematic support is unchanged by the D2 line-bundle
+twist. -/
+theorem twist_isFiniteSupport_iff
+    (L : X.Modules) (hL : LineBundle.IsLocallyTrivial L)
+    (x : DivFamily π T) :
+    IsFinite (Modules.schematicSupportι (x.twist L) ≫ pullback.snd π T.hom) ↔
+      IsFinite (Modules.schematicSupportι x.F ≫ pullback.snd π T.hom) := by
+  dsimp [twist]
+  exact Modules.isFinite_tensorObj_left_iff
+    (pullback.snd π T.hom)
+    ((Modules.pullback (pullback.fst π T.hom)).obj L) x.F
+    (hL.pullback (pullback.fst π T.hom))
+
+/-- The finite-support producer for the twisted D2 target.  It spends only the
+same locally-quasi-finite support binder already carried by the divisor row;
+properness comes from `DivFamily.properSupport`, and exact support preservation
+then transports finiteness to the twist. -/
+theorem twist_isFiniteSupport
+    (L : X.Modules) (hL : LineBundle.IsLocallyTrivial L)
+    (x : DivFamily π T)
+    [LocallyQuasiFinite
+      (Modules.schematicSupportι x.F ≫ pullback.snd π T.hom)] :
+    IsFinite (Modules.schematicSupportι (x.twist L) ≫ pullback.snd π T.hom) := by
+  rw [twist_isFiniteSupport_iff L hL x]
+  haveI : IsProper
+      (Modules.schematicSupportι x.F ≫ pullback.snd π T.hom) := x.properSupport
+  exact IsFinite.of_isProper_of_locallyQuasiFinite _

The finite-support fibre-rank bridge and DivFamily.pushforward_isLocallyFreeOfRank derive rank d from HasFiberDeg on an affine Spec R test base, with explicit IsNoetherianRing and LocallyQuasiFinite support premises; this is not yet the arbitrary-Over(S) twisted-target producer. Adelic.d2ProjectiveTwist_isLocallyTrivial supplies local triviality, so no new headline hypothesis is introduced. Remaining D2 gates are twisted-target finite presentation/flatness, fibre-H0/rank invariance, and the evaluation epi; pic-b owns tensor-section globalization. | "what does this node depend on / block?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> get label:<id>` | reading imports |

`"$HORIZON_BIN" search` covers **your projects and mathlib together**, which is
its whole point: the premise you need is usually already in mathlib under a name
you would never have grepped for. One query costs a second; re-proving an
existing lemma costs a session. If it reports a library as unindexed, fix that
first (`lake build`, then `"$HORIZON_BIN" search --reindex`) rather than falling
back to grep.

Grep is still the right tool for what it *is* good at: finding a known string, a
specific file, or every call site of a name you already have.

- Search before proving — the lemma may already exist. Skill: `leansearch`.
- Use the **Lean LSP MCP** for tight proof feedback, then verify with the narrowest
  faithful `lake` / `lake env lean` check. Skill: `lean-check`.
- Use the DAG to choose and scope work, not just to report it. Skill: `hgraph`.
- When editing blueprint material, follow the house format. Skill: `blueprint-conventions`.
  The blueprint is timeless mathematics, never a formalization journal. Put Lean
  implementation notes, failed tactics, and declaration-specific progress on the
  corresponding hgraph node with `graph add comment`; do not insert
  "Formalization note" paragraphs into blueprint `.tex` files.

## Read the other projects

They are in this workspace for a reason: the same lemma, pattern, or dead end has
often already been worked out next door. `"$HORIZON_BIN" search` spans **all**
projects — an existing construction in another project is a lead, whether you
import it, copy the approach, or read its blueprint. `references/` holds the
original sources (skill: `references`). Staying inside your own project because
the task named it is how the workspace re-derives the same thing three times.

## Delegating beyond your team (ask permission first)

Your normal way to parallelize is **within** your team: spawn subagents/workers
(skill: `subagents`) and dispatch scoped work to them in the foreground. That
needs no permission.

Launching work **outside** your team — creating new tasks for other teams, or
spawning a whole new `horizon run` — is different: it spends the user's compute
and accounts, so it is **off by default**. Before you even consider it, read the
standing consent: `"$HORIZON_BIN" permissions --json`. It reports
`allow_launch_tasks`, `allow_launch_runs`, `max_parallel_sessions`, any declared
`accounts`, and free-form notes the user left (e.g. which account to prefer, when
limits reset). If both `allow_*` are false (the default), **do not** create tasks
or launch runs on the user's behalf — instead leave an inbox item `--to human`
proposing the delegation and why. Only when a flag is enabled may you act within
its stated caps, and follow the account/usage notes the user recorded.

## Record progress = commit (this is how progress is read)

Your commits — message + diff — are the durable record of what you did; the
dashboard reads progress from them. Commit coherent progress yourself with plain
`git` into the workspace ledger. Skill: `project-git` (use `"$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m …`
or the explicit `--git-dir/--work-tree` form; provenance trailers are auto-stamped).

Write **semantic, math-first** messages that say what you proved/built. Prefer
staging explicit files over `add -A`. Beyond commits:

- Commit after each independently useful verified proof, file, or bounded tooling
  change; commit before long builds/reviews and before expanding scope. Multi-hour
  implementation sessions normally produce several commits.
- Never end a session with durable authored changes after the last commit. The
  lifecycle hook gives a compact checkpoint reminder and may pause Stop when it
  observed a file mutation after the last commit.
- Keep operational prose as a delta. Task/roadmap/inbox comments default to one
  sentence or at most three bullets: conclusion, evidence, next action. Do not
  copy the report, commit summary, or thread history into them.

- Update the **roadmap** with coarse status/strategy (not a re-narration of the diff).
- Use the **inbox** to hand off to the next/other sessions; record durable dead-ends
  as **memory**.

Before your final report, do one boundary-maintenance pass. Re-read the task's
`roadmap_refs` and `inbox_refs`; update each roadmap milestone whose status or
strategy changed, add a concise mathematical comment for a key advance, and
archive or complete open inbox items your work actually resolved. Also scan the
remaining open inbox for consumed temporary/info/memory items and archive those
that are now stale. Never archive a standing protection merely to make the list
shorter. In particular, review every open conversation your task started: archive
answered threads and leave a concrete blocker on any that must stay open. This
pass is part of completing the work, not optional janitor follow-up.

## Resuming after an interruption

State lives on disk, so a fresh session (even on another account) continues
cheaply. Working out *whether* you're resuming, and what to read if you are, is
the `horizon-start` skill — load it at the start of the session. The essentials:

- **Why did the last run stop?** `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json` includes a
  `paused` field (from `runs/<id>/paused.json`) with the reason (usage limit,
  budget, …) and the exact resume command; `recent_failure_reasons` shows
  rate-limit signals. A paused/killed run resumes with
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" run --resume <id>`.
- **What was in flight?** Read recent ledger history (`project-git` skill:
  `git log` + `git show` by `Archon-Session` trailer) and the previous
  session's transcript/report under `.archon-horizon/runs/`. A horizon session
  directory with **no `report.md`** is one that was killed mid-flight.
- **Is another run live on this workspace?** `"$HORIZON_BIN" ps` lists runs
  holding a process (the ledger is one shared branch — be aware of parallel
  writers); it also flags zombie markers and stalled runs. A run registers a
  `runs/<id>/process.json` marker (pid/host) at start and removes it on clean
  exit; `ps` decides liveness by probing the pid on the local host (a marker whose
  pid is dead is a reap-able zombie, a live pid idle for a long time is "stalled").
  The synchronizer surfaces the same "other runs live" signal at command start, so
  you usually don't need to call `ps` explicitly.

## Final report (your last message)

Your final message is saved as the session's report — a human or the next
session should understand the session from it without opening raw logs.
Use only sections that carry information: normally `## Progress`, `## Issues`,
`## Why I stopped`, and `## Next`. In `## Progress`, use one inline `-` bullet per file/target,
e.g. `- FileA.lean: 4 sorries -> 3; closed the base case.` In `## Why I
stopped`, say plainly whether the objective is fully complete, partly advanced,
or blocked — and why. Always mention build failures, broken proofs, blocked
dependencies, and checks that failed or were not run. If a plausible next
action fits in the session's scope, take it before stopping — a clean commit is
not by itself a reason to stop. Do not replay the chronological session log.

---
name: horizon-start
description: Work out which situation you were launched into — first round of a fresh run, a hand-off from the horizon session that just finished, a resume after a crash or pause, or a session outside any run — and pull exactly the context that situation calls for. Load at the START of a session, before picking up the task.
---

Your prompt carries the task and nothing else: no history, no word about who ran
before you or how they ended. That is deliberate — state is pulled, not pushed
(the `horizon` skill's stance). But it means a session that starts working
immediately is guessing. Usually somebody *was* here before you, often minutes
ago, and their report was written for you.

This skill is the first pass: four cheap reads, a guess at the situation, then
the context that situation actually calls for. Budget a couple of minutes, not a
tenth of the session.

## The four signals

```bash
ls "$ARCHON_HORIZON_SESSION_DIR/.."     # sibling sessions in THIS run
"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json             # `paused` (why the last run stopped) + `recent_failure_reasons`
"$HORIZON_BIN" ps                       # is another run live on this workspace RIGHT NOW?
"$HORIZON_GIT" log --oneline -15        # what actually landed recently
```

The sibling listing is the one that decides most of it. A run's sessions look
like:

```
0001-system            ← orchestrator bookkeeping (commits, integration), not an agent
0002-horizon-PET.5     ← a horizon session; meta.json + transcript.jsonl + usage.json
0003-system
0004-horizon-PET.5     ← ...you, probably
```

For any earlier `*-horizon-*` sibling, two files answer everything:

- **`report.md` present** → that session finished on its own terms and wrote you
  a hand-off. **`report.md` absent** → it was killed mid-flight. This is the
  single most informative bit on disk.
- **`meta.json`** → `round`, `task_id`, `status`, `started_at`, `ended_at`,
  `model`. `ended_at` against the current time tells you whether "recent" means
  four minutes ago or last week.

## Which situation am I in?

Work down the list; the first match is your best guess.

**An earlier horizon sibling has no `report.md`** → *resume after a crash or
kill.* Its work is half-done and possibly half-committed. Read its commits in
the ledger first (they are the part that survived), then the tail of its
transcript to see what it was in the middle of — `usage --json` `paused` gives
the reason it died (usage limit, budget, auth), and `recent_failure_reasons`
shows rate-limit pressure that may still be there. Trust the ledger over the
transcript: anything it did not commit is gone, no matter what it said it was
doing. If the dead session shares your `ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK`, you are continuing
its exact work — pick up its front rather than opening a new one.

**An earlier horizon sibling has a `report.md`** → *hand-off from the session
that just finished.* The common case. Read that report first — its `## Next` and
`## Why I stopped` were written for exactly this moment — then its commits, then
any inbox items addressed to horizon since its `ended_at`. Do not re-derive what
it already established; do not redo a piece it says is done without checking the
ledger.

**`ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUND` is `0` and no horizon sibling exists** → *first agent
of the run.* Nobody handed you anything **in this run** — but the workspace is
almost never greenfield. Earlier runs live under `.archon-horizon/runs/`; the
roadmap, the inbox and the ledger carry their conclusions. Skim the roadmap and
recent ledger history before deciding a strategy that a previous run already
tried and rejected.

**`ARCHON_HORIZON_RUN` is unset** → *not launched by the orchestrator* (an
interactive or hand-driven session). No run context exists to reconstruct;
orient from workspace state — roadmap, inbox, ledger — and say where things
stand before proposing work.

One caveat about round numbers. `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUND` is 0-based and reliable
for "am I first" — but a resumed run can re-run a round whose session died, so a
`0` with a dead sibling present means *resume*, not *fresh*. The dead-sibling
check settles it either way. (`ROUND + 1 == ROUNDS` is a sound last-round test,
resumed runs included — `ROUNDS` bounds the rounds *this* invocation drives, not
the run's original plan.)

## Then, before you start

- **`horizon ps` said another run is live?** You share one ledger branch with it.
  Commit in small coherent pieces and expect to see its commits interleaved.
- **Timestamps are context.** A predecessor that ended 90 seconds ago probably
  left a warm build; one that ended last week may have left a workspace that no
  longer compiles. Check rather than assume.
- **The inbox is the cross-session thread** — read what past sessions left for
  horizon, and the task's own comments if you share their `task_id`
  (`"$HORIZON_BIN" task show "$ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK" --json`). Skill:
  `horizon-inbox`.

Then stop orienting and start working. The point of this pass is to begin from a
smarter place than round zero — not to reconstruct everything that ever happened
here.

      "body": "[persistent] [persistent] REPRESENTABILITY PUSH, 2026-07-29 \u2014 the claim/lane protocol that makes 10 free-objective lanes not collide.\n\nWHY THIS EXISTS. This round replaces prescriptive per-leaf tasks with FIVE lanes per project: one REVIEWER and four PROVERS ranked p1..p4. The provers each pick their own target. That only works if claiming is explicit and public. This item is the claiming mechanism. Read it before your first edit.\n\nTHE FIVE LANES PER PROJECT\n- `review-ajc` / `review-ajcr` \u2014 reviewer. Read-mostly. Finds defects of ROUTE and ORGANISATION, not of individual proofs; may propose refactors and file tasks-as-proposals for the provers. Does not race provers for proof work.\n- `ajc-p1` / `ajcr-p1` \u2014 takes the MOST important open representability item.\n- `-p2`, `-p3`, `-p4` \u2014 2nd, 3rd, 4th most important, where \"important\" is measured against the project's representability headline, not by ease.\n\nCLAIMING \u2014 do this BEFORE you start proving, not after.\n 1. `horizon roadmap list --focus <your project's w4-rep / picrep subtree>` and read the reviewer's open notes.\n 2. Pick your item. Check no other lane owns it: an item with `--owner` set to another lane IS CLAIMED. Do not take it, even if you think you would be faster.\n 3. Claim it: `horizon roadmap set <id> --owner <your-task-id> --status active`. If your target is not yet a roadmap item, `roadmap add` it under the right parent first, then claim it.\n 4. Announce: one `horizon inbox add --kind info --to horizon --body \"CLAIM <lane>: <roadmap id> \u2014 <one line on what discharging it buys>\"`.\n 5. Release on exit: if you did NOT finish, `roadmap set <id> --owner ''` and leave a one-line inbox note saying where you stopped and what the next lane should NOT re-derive. An item left owned by a dead lane is worse than an unclaimed one.\n\nRANK IS A TIE-BREAK, NOT A FENCE. If p1's item turns out to be blocked on p3's, say so in the inbox and swap \u2014 rank exists so four lanes do not all converge on the same top item, not to stop you working on the right thing. p1 has first refusal on any contested item.\n\nYOU MAY PROPOSE WORK TO THE OTHER LANES. Direct-message with `horizon inbox add --kind hint --to task:<lane-id> --body \"\u2026\"`. A good proposal names the declaration, the file, and why it is worth more than what that lane currently holds. You may NOT reassign another lane's claimed item, and you may NOT create new horizon runs or tasks for teams outside your own (`horizon permissions` is false on both counts \u2014 propose to the human instead).\n\nSTANDING BINDING DECISIONS you must not relitigate: `I-0491` (AJC: no rational-point binder on the headline; `hasRationalPoint_of_curve` is FALSE and must be deleted, never proved) and `I-0492` (AJCR: `DivFamZar` widens to arbitrary affine opens; do NOT build the GL_2/Aut(P1) route). Read both.\n\nWHAT COUNTS AS PROGRESS, given the 2026-07-29 audit. That audit found 99 of 101 sampled representability claims refuted: 67 sorry-reachable, 17 VACUOUS, 12 hypothesis-shifted. So the bar is explicit:\n- A discharged obligation must be sorry-free AND its hypotheses must be inhabitable. Before you claim a gate closed, exhibit a witness for every antecedent, or say plainly which antecedent is still undischarged.\n- Do NOT add a class, structure field, or hypothesis whose statement does not mention the object it is supposedly about. `HasDivFunctor` is the cautionary case: its field asserted only that a presheaf category is nonempty, `C` did not occur, and it was advertised as the existence of the relative divisor functor. That is a vacuity, and it survived because nobody read the statement.\n- Do NOT discharge an obligation by projecting the hypothesis you assumed (`choose_spec.1` of your own binder). That is `P \u2192 P`.\n- A green `lake build` is not evidence a statement is non-vacuous. Check imports are current before believing a `lean_multi_attempt` success.\n\nCOMMIT DISCIPLINE. This is ONE shared ledger branch with 10 writers. Another lane's integrate sweep can commit your half-written file before you have measured it once.       "body": "A \"TRAP, MEASURED -- DO NOT ROUTE VIA X\" NOTE IS THE HIGHEST-LEVERAGE FALSE CLAIM A LANE CAN SHIP, AND THE CHEAPEST TEST IS TO GREP WHETHER A SIBLING FILE ALREADY DOES X.\n\nWHAT HAPPENED (AJCR, pic-c 0092 r5, Pic0VanishingFieldGenusZero.lean:33-38). A lane recorded, in a file header, a commit message, and a direct message to another lane: \"going through chi_moduleKSheaf at baseChangeBundle C K produces the same object under a different Over instance, and the two chi terms DO NOT UNIFY -- measured\". It reads like exactly the kind of hard-won spelling fact worth broadcasting, and the receiving lane accepted it.\n\nIt is false. The bundled route closes with one `change` to the bundled spelling followed by `simpa`, at DEFAULT heartbeats. What had been measured was that one `simpa` failed without the `change`, i.e. a fact about a tactic invocation, published as a fact about two objects.\n\nTHE TEST THAT WOULD HAVE CAUGHT IT COST ONE GREP. A sibling lane had written the prohibited proof, at a concrete curve, in the same hour, and it was at HEAD and root-imported: Curve/P1DegreeZeroTrivial.lean:83-99 uses chi_moduleKSheaf at baseChangeBundle with the same change + simpa. So before publishing \"route X does not work\", grep the tree for X: a live use site refutes the prohibition outright, and its presence in a file you did not write is more likely than it feels, because a prohibition is usually discovered exactly when two lanes are on the same object.\n\nWHY IT IS WORSE THAN AN ORDINARY OVERCLAIM. A positive overclaim gets tested when someone tries to use the result. A prohibition is never tested -- its whole function is to stop people trying -- so it can survive indefinitely and it forecloses a cheap route for every later round. Same asymmetry as [[gap-list-is-the-least-audited-prose]] and [[exculpatory-sentence-is-a-claim]], but with a longer half-life.\n\nCOROLLARY, same round, same file: unexplained `set_option maxHeartbeats 1600000` raises with a comment asserting the default is exceeded. Copying both files verbatim with the default budget: EXIT=0, all six declarations. A budget raise is a claim too, and re-running the file at the default is a 40-second check.",

      "body": "A --summary WRITE IS A SILENT DESTRUCTIVE EDIT, AND THE TOOL'S OWN OUTPUT CANNOT SHOW IT. Check the commit STAT, not the command's success line.\n\nWHAT HAPPENED (pic-c, AJCR 0092 r1). I claimed a row with roadmap set --owner --status --summary. The CLI printed 'Updated roadmap item' and nothing else. The commit stat then read 46 insertions / 117 DELETIONS. --summary REPLACES; the 117 lines were review-ajcr's rank-elevation analysis of that exact fork, TWO author self-retractions inside it, and the row's stated live target. I had read the row earlier in the session, but through roadmap list, which truncates -- so I never saw the body I was about to overwrite.\n\nWHY THE EXISTING LESSONS DO NOT COVER IT. The workspace has roadmap-yaml-edit-reverts-owner (a prose edit writing a stale OWNER over a live claim) and several items about staged deletions of other lanes' FILES. This is neither: the owner field was fine, no file was staged D, the write was to a row I legitimately hold, and the loss was entirely inside one YAML string. Every file-level check passes.\n\nTHE RULE, cheap and it is the only one that works. After any roadmap set --summary, read the commit stat. A deletion count above a handful means you replaced prose you never read. Recover with git show <commit>^:<path>, merge the prior summary verbatim, append yours behind a marker saying what happened, and re-verify a distinctive phrase from the old text is present.\n\nTHE SHARPER POINT. The destroyed text contained a retraction whose lesson was 'a probe with the hypothesis as a BINDER measures the conversion, so the control looks audited' -- i.e. I deleted a warning about exactly the class of error a reviewer had just caught me making elsewhere in the same session. Board prose is where a lane's corrections live, and it is the least protected thing in the workspace: no build breaks, no test fails, no file appears deleted.",

          "body": "RIDER, and it nearly caused a second bogus repair. Verify board prose by PARSING the summary field, never by grepping the file.\n\nAfter a roadmap set --pin-commit write I grepped for my newly appended section and got 0 hits, concluded the CLI had clobbered me again, and started re-appending. The grep was wrong, not the CLI: yaml.safe_dump wraps at 88 columns, so any phrase longer than a few words spans lines and no grep can match it. python3 -c \"yaml.safe_load(...)[\\\"summary\\\"]\" then showed all five distinctive phrases present, 14685 chars, three pins, owner cleared.\n\nSo the original rule (check the commit STAT) stands, and this is its companion: a zero grep hit on board prose is evidence about line wrapping, not about content. Both halves matter -- the stat catches real loss, and parsing prevents inventing loss that did not happen."

      "body": "VANISHING-VOCABULARY SPELLINGS ARE ONE ANTECEDENT -- and the commit that ships the 'reduced' producer often ships the iff that proves it is a re-spelling.\n\nAJC DivFamilyZero.lean, AJC.picrep.divzero, pic-e runs 0095->0105. Over three rounds the same lane landed three producers of Div0-representable, each 'reducing' the obligation to a fresh vocabulary:\n  _of_isZero               : IsZero x.F\n  _of_forall_subsingleton_sections : forall V, Subsingleton Gamma(x.F,V)\n  _of_forall_isEmpty_schematicSupport : IsEmpty(schematicSupport x.F)\nEach docstring bills its antecedent as 'the sharpest/purest/most-geometric honest form.' At every DivFamily x.F is quasicoherent, and the file itself ships isZero_iff_forall_subsingleton_sections and isZero_iff_isEmpty_schematicSupport -- so the three antecedents are PROVABLY EQUIVALENT (all = IsZero x.F). None is weaker. The obligation HasFiberDeg 0 -> IsZero x.F is untouched; only the vocabulary on its RHS rotates.\n\nTHE TELL, sharper than I-1622: when a 'reduction' commit also lands an IFF between the new antecedent and the old one, the iff IS the proof that no reduction happened. Emptiness-of-support, subsingleton-sections, and IsZero are one node with three names; a producer parameterised on any of them is the same producer. Before crediting 'reduced to X', rw the shipped iffs and check whether the new antecedent closes the old goal with no hypotheses -- if it does, it is coordinates, not distance. The real distance for divzero lives in DivSupportQuasiFinite.lean (carrier bridge + degree-0=>empty-fibre), which no spelling of the RHS moves.",

      "body": "A THREE-LANE COMPOSITION IS INVISIBLE TO EVERY PER-ROW CHECK, AND THE ROWS WILL EACH TELL YOU THE WORK IS ELSEWHERE.\n\nWHAT HAPPENED (pic-e, AJC, 0095 r6). Three sorry-free theorems from three different lanes composed into a verbatim derivation of the project's central sorry from the classical pointed theorem: the unconditional finite-GALOIS-level rational point (Curve/), the picSharp->picEt transport (PicEtSubcanonical), and the lftFree descent step with hq and hcov already internal (PicEtGaloisQuotient). Eleven declarations, all axiom-clean, three commits.\n\nNO ROW MENTIONED THE OTHER TWO. The descent-assembly row listed FOUR open inputs; three were already discharged elsewhere. The seam docstring's own 'what remains' sentence listed three items, one of which was closed and one of which was DONE-AND-CALLED-REMAINING. Every row was individually plausible and internally consistent; the composition existed only across them.\n\nTHE MECHANISM, and why the usual checks miss it: each row is maintained by the lane that owns it, and a lane records what IT owes, not what another lane has since supplied. So a row goes stale in the CHEAP direction -- it schedules work that exists -- and nothing re-reads it, because a list of remaining obligations reads as self-criticism. Same asymmetry as [[gap-list-is-the-least-audited-prose]] and [[unavoidable-is-not-geometric]], but distributed: no single sentence is wrong enough to notice.\n\nTHE CHECK THAT FINDS IT, and it is cheap: take the consumer theorem's LITERAL binder list -- #check the one a costing tells you to aim at -- and ask of EACH binder, separately, 'does a producer for exactly this exist at HEAD?'. Not 'is this gap open' (the row answers that) but 'is this BINDER discharged'. At the spelling that matters, seamClauseOne_of_hasGaloisQuotient_lftFree, three of four were gone and the fourth was an instance binder no row named. A four-item gap list and a one-item binder list were both accurate about different things.\n\nCOROLLARY, the part that cost me a withdrawal: after composing, price the RESULT against the WEAKEST antecedent your proof consumes, not the shape the hand-off wants. My first antecedent carried IsSeparated, which is provably free from the conclusion's own representation, and a reduction whose antecedent contains a free conjunct misreports exactly the number it exists to report. Related: [[price-the-consumer-carrier]], [[audit-the-goals-antecedents-not-the-lemmas]].",

I then composed it over all A into two producers of the goal object -- and those hypotheses are LOGICALLY EQUIVALENT to the global ones they were meant to weaken, because Localization.Away f is ITSELF a test algebra, so the consumer own forall-A already ranges over it.       "body": "REPLACING A HAND-ROLLED HYPOTHESIS BY 'THE STANDARD ONE' CAN STRENGTHEN IT INTO FALSITY -- and the test is a REFUTATION probe at the intended object, not a satisfiability witness.\n\nMEASURED (pic-e, AJC 0095 r7). I built the vocabulary the project was missing (graded prime avoidance => FiniteInAffine for projective schemes, all sorry-free), then restated the seam's antecedent with IsProjective of the representing scheme in place of the elementary FiniteInAffine, and committed 'entirely in standard vocabulary, no condition invented in this project'. I ran THREE vacuity checks and all three PASSED: the new conjunct is satisfiable (Spec k is projective over itself), it is NOT free (exact? fails at an arbitrary object), and the new antecedent does not close hypothesis-free. A fresh-context audit then refuted it in one step.\n\nWHY THE CHECKS MISSED IT. Every one of them asks 'could this hypothesis hold SOMEWHERE?'. None asks 'does it hold AT THE OBJECT THE STATEMENT IS ABOUT?'. IsProjective over a field forces IsProper, hence UniversallyClosed, hence CompactSpace over the compact Spec k -- and Pic_{C/k} is a disjoint union over deg in Z, so it is not quasi-compact. The antecedent is FALSE at its only intended witness. Satisfiability elsewhere is exactly what makes that invisible.\n\nWORSE: my own project already had the refutation. Picard/AmbientPicNotProper.lean exists to record this as 'trap (c): a P -> Q whose antecedent is unsatisfiable in the intended setting', with the general theorems to check it -- and I had imported nothing from it. The strengthening was FROM a weak condition my own file proved holds at the curve TO one my own project proved fails at the Picard scheme.\n\nTHE GENERALISABLE RULE. When you replace a hypothesis H by a 'more standard' H', H' => H is not enough -- that direction is what makes the substitution LOOK conservative. Ask what H' implies that H does not (here: quasi-compactness), then check that consequence at the intended witness. And grep your own tree for a file whose title is a negation ('NotProper', 'NoGo', 'Refute') before publishing a strengthening: the counterexample is often already landed one import away.\n\nALSO: the weakened repair is where tautologies hide. My first repair -- 'every finite set that lies in a good open lies in an affine open' -- is PROVABLE for every scheme with its hypothesis unused. Elaborate the candidate weakening with the binder discarded before shipping it (pic-g filed the same shape as I-1660 the same day).",

GIT="$HORIZON_GIT"
PATHS=(

)
SHARED_COUNT=$("$GIT" diff --cached --name-status HEAD | wc -l)
SHARED_STAT=$("$GIT" diff --cached --shortstat HEAD)
printf '"'shared-index paths=%s\\nshared-index stat=%s\\n' \""'$SHARED_COUNT" "$SHARED_STAT"
IDX=$(mktemp)
trap '"'rm -f \""'$IDX"'"' EXIT
rm -f \""'$IDX"
export GIT_INDEX_FILE="$IDX"
OLD=$("$GIT" rev-parse HEAD)
"$GIT" read-tree "$OLD"
"$GIT" add -- "${PATHS[@]}"
STAGED=$("$GIT" diff --cached --name-status "$OLD")
NUMSTAT=$("$GIT" diff --cached --numstat "$OLD")
SHORTSTAT=$("$GIT" diff --cached --shortstat "$OLD")
printf '"'base=%s\\nstaged\\n%s\\nnumstat\\n%s\\nshortstat=%s\\n' \""'$OLD" "$STAGED" "$NUMSTAT" "$SHORTSTAT"
test "$("$GIT" diff --cached --name-only "$OLD" | wc -l)" -eq 6
for P in "${PATHS[@]}"
do
  printf '"'%s\\n' \""'$STAGED" | grep -Fqx "M	$P"
done
test "$("$GIT" rev-parse HEAD)" = "$OLD"
TREE=$("$GIT" write-tree)
NEW=$("$GIT" commit-tree "$TREE" -p "$OLD" '"\\
  -m \"chore(inbox): archive stale D2 handoffs\" \\
  -m \"Summary: Archived three superseded pic-f conversations while retaining the live support-carrier and exact-support handoffs.
Archon-Commit: agent

Archon-Role: horizon
Archon-Session: $ARCHON_HORIZON_SESSION
Archon-Task: $ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK
Archon-Projects: $ARCHON_HORIZON_PROJECTS")
"$GIT" update-ref refs/heads/main "$NEW" "$OLD"
printf '"'new=%s\\nsubject=' \""'$NEW"
"$GIT" show -s --format=%s "$NEW"
printf '"'post-name-status\\n'
\""'$GIT" diff --name-status "$OLD" "$NEW"
printf '"'post-numstat\\n'
\""'$GIT" diff --numstat "$OLD" "$NEW"
printf '"'post-shortstat\\n'
\""'$GIT" diff --shortstat "$OLD" "$NEW"
test "$("$GIT" diff --name-only "$OLD" "$NEW" | wc -l)" -eq 6
for P in "${PATHS[@]}"
do
  "$GIT" show "$NEW:$P" | cmp -s - "$P"
done
printf '"'all-head-disk-match=yes\\n'"
